reason: Phaedrus's 2026-11-03 delivery directive makes each slice useful alone and proved on its own running consumer path before merge. Independent slices can proceed in parallel; CI and one critical-correctness/security review gate deployment, not merge.

edits.before: description: "Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer."
edits.after: description: "For initiatives, migrations and stacked changes, choose complete slices useful alone, prove each on its real running consumer path before merge, and sequence only actual dependencies."

edits.before: Order work as a sequence of small units, each ending in a state you can check, and don't advance until the current one is green.
edits.after: Shape the whole initiative's outcome, then choose the smallest atomically shippable slices. Each improves its consumer's real path and keeps main working. Sequence actual dependencies; independent slices with disjoint ownership can proceed in parallel.

edits.before: **Why:** A break caught at the unit that caused it is cheap to localize. A break caught after a batch is buried, and you have already built further on a broken base. Sequencing those same units into a delivery a reviewer can replay turns "trust me" into "watch it go red, then green."
edits.after: **Why:** A break caught in its slice is cheap to localize. Infrastructure alone is not a useful slice unless it supplies a usable consumer contract. A small change that breaks an existing path is reckless, not small.

edits.before: **Execution.** In a sweep, migration, or any run of similar edits, verify each change before starting the next. Each unit is a before/after bracket: known-good state, one change, run the check, then proceed. Rebase onto clean trunk first so every check measures against the real baseline. When a lever does the edits, the per-unit check is nearly free. Run it anyway.
edits.after: **Execution.** Give each slice an owner, bounded diff, preserved behavior, a concrete risk check and an outside Oracle on the real running app or actual consumer boundary. Use one [Boat worker](../boat-workers/SKILL.md) per slice. Build the complete path and drive it through [Verification](../verification/SKILL.md) before merge; add its canonical formal-property checks for ordering, concurrency or durability. Capture comparable before/after proof and reject the relevant defect, not merely a convenient unit-test fixture. Each owner verifies its own path; dependent slices start from that demonstrated result.

edits.before: **Delivery.** Stack commits and PRs in the order that proves the work. The canonical shape is the failing test first, then the fix on top. Other story orders are a subtraction before the reshape, a baseline capture before the treatment, the scaffold before the feature. Each commit lands on its own and the sequence reads as an argument.
edits.after: **Delivery.** Order commits so the argument can be replayed: behavior pin before reshape, failing check before repair, proven shared primitive before consumers. Merge a complete verified slice without CI, independent review or a judge as merge gates. Follow [ship-loop](../ship-loop/SKILL.md): fast CI and one review limited to critical correctness and security run only at the pre-deploy release gate, then deploy and check the live journey. Done when every slice is worth merging alone and has its own observed real-path proof.
